meanings: adjective: most frequent or common
examples: The predominant color in the paint was white, even though the name "morning sun" made it sound yellow.

meanings: verb: to grow strong and healthy
examples: The gardener was pleased to find that his new plants only needed a small amount of sunshine and water to thrive and grow quickly.

meanings: verb: to meet and discuss before deciding
examples: Before I invite you to join our secret club, I'll have to confer with the other members and get their approval.

meanings: adjective: near or close but not necessarily touching
examples: The owners of the two adjacent shops worked together to clean up the alley that separated their buildings.

meanings: adjective: having a strong, good smell
examples: Shirley loved growing roses because they were much more fragrant than the other, more dull smelling flowers in her garden.

meanings: adjective: experienced through a second person
examples: Without money, Ben had to settle for the vicarious experience of watching the host of his favorite TV show travel to many exciting countries.

meanings: verb: to be made of
examples: Although most of the former state is now part of Russia, the Soviet Union comprised fifteen now independent countries.

meanings: verb: to delay or pause in order to get more time
examples: When asked to marry a man she didn't love, Charlotte stalled by faking a sudden coughing fit that prevented her from talking.

meanings: adjective: not normal
examples: According to those who don't believe in climate change, the extreme weather over the last five years is simply anomalous and won't continue for long.

meanings: adjective: easy to see
examples: "Just my luck!" said Sam, whose forehead had grown a conspicuous pimple the day before the school dance.

meanings: verb: to attach or tie tightly to something (not using glue)
examples: The dog's owner made sure to fasten the leash to a nearby tree with a strong knot to make sure it didn't escape again.

meanings: noun: the material or method used, especially for communication and art
examples: The artist used finger paint as his medium to remind the viewer of childhood.

meanings: verb: to cause to continue
examples: If you do not let him do things for himself, you are merely perpetuating bad habits that will be even harder to break in the future.

meanings: verb: to produce or cause after a process
examples: Sam was concerned that four heads of lettuce wouldn't be enough, but he was pleased when his salad yielded enough for all thirty people at the party.

meanings: adjective: common throughout a wide area at a certain time
examples: The virus was most prevalent in humid areas where mosquitoes were common and could pass it from person to person.

meanings: verb: to choose not to do (used for enjoyable but possibly harmful actions)
examples: My uncle Ethan was in a car accident in college while driving home from a party, and he has abstained from alcohol ever since.

meanings: adjective: uneven and sharp
examples: Dave was sure he could have climbed higher if he hadn't cut his hands on the jagged edges of the cliff face.

meanings: adjective: difficult and requiring a lot of effort
examples: I don't think I'd make a good triathlete: I find swimming and cycling easy enough, but I find running absolutely arduous.

meanings: verb: to become involved in order to stop or change a bad situation
examples: Unless we intervene soon, climate change may cause massive damage to cities around the world.

meanings: verb: to prove to be false or incorrect
examples: Newly found videos of the security guard sleeping during the robbery at the shopping mall refute his story of having chased the thief.

meanings: verb: to happen as a result
examples: If a cut isn't cleaned and treated quickly, an infection may ensue.

meanings: verb: to lead and be sure something is done correctly
examples: The chief engineer oversaw the development of the new computer chip, making sure that each part of the design fit into the overall plan.

meanings: adjective: longer in one direction
examples: The huge, oblong table was set for ten people: four on each side, and one on each end.

meanings: noun: an area that is higher at one end and lower at the other
examples: Many houses in San Francisco are built on sharp inclines, so some buildings have three floors on one side but only two on the other.

meanings: verb: to not be caught
examples: The infamous art thief had eluded the police once more, but he still had not found a buyer for the stolen painting.

meanings: verb: to get after special effort to find
examples: The chef made every effort to procure the rare vegetables for his wife's favorite dish as a gift for their 30th wedding anniversary.

meanings: adjective: giving a feeling that something bad will happen
examples: Dark skies and lightning loomed over the town constantly, leaving the residents with an ominous feeling and fear of the weather.

meanings: adjective: moving quickly and lightly
examples: After training for months with heavy weights on their backs, the team immediately felt more agile as soon as the weights were removed.

meanings: adjective: only (used to show large amounts of one thing having an effect)
examples: The sheer size of the Amazon river makes it very difficult to cross at some points.

meanings: noun: a very small amount
examples: After examining the crime scene, the detectives knew they were dealing with professional thieves — not a single shred of evidence was left behind.

meanings: verb: to weaken (usually paired with an abstract term)
examples: William undermined the teacher's authority by questioning her judgment on numerous occasions.

meanings: adjective: very obvious, without trying to hide (used for bad things)
examples: Vincent's blatant disregard for the rules got him into a lot of trouble at his strict private school.

meanings: adjective: existing from birth, not learned
examples: Languages have been created in every culture because humans have an innate need to communicate.

meanings: verb: to contain or include
examples: At many universities, the pre-med courses are subsumed in the Biology department rather than given a department of their own.

meanings: adjective: belonging to the most basic nature of something, impossible to remove
examples: In the past, when we used gold and silver, money had far more intrinsic value than the paper we use today.

meanings: noun: an absence of emotion or enthusiasm
examples: The hardest part of teaching high-school math is fighting apathy in my students—or for that matter, keeping them awake at all.

meanings: noun: a color
examples: We watched from our campsite on top of the mountain as the sun set and changed the hue of the sky to the colors of a peach.

meanings: adjective: sad and boring or colorless
examples: The party was a dreary affair: only five people showed up, and none of them could find much to talk about.

meanings: noun: an event resulting in a lot of loss or pain
examples: "It's just jewelry," said Frank, but to Augusta, the loss of her favorite necklace was a calamity.

meanings: verb: to grow in number quickly
examples: When the researchers left for lunch, they counted 200 bacteria in the sample; afterward, the microbes had proliferated to over 4000.

meanings: adjective: in or relating to the countryside, away from cities
examples: Ron preferred to live outside the city, as he had grown up near a lake surrounded by a forest in the more rural part of his hometown.

meanings: adjective: possibly true, realistic
examples: After recordings of the president discussing the illegal actions of his advisors became public, it no longer seemed plausible that he was blameless.

meanings: adjective: likely to do or happen (with "to," used for negative effects)
examples: "Secure that tent," said the camp leader, "or it's liable to blow away in the wind."

meanings: verb: to stop doing
examples: The lawyer warned the new hamburger restaurant that they would be sued if they did not desist all use of the copy of the McDonald's logo.

meanings: verb: to run away from danger
examples: The sight of a shadow crossing over the ground causes many animals to flee in case there is a predator flying above.

meanings: verb: to not be caught; to avoid
examples: The burglars evaded the police by driving as quickly as they could through a narrow and twisting road.

meanings: adjective: sleepy
examples: The day dragged on, and the only thing keeping the workers from getting drowsy was the automatically refilling coffee machine.

meanings: noun: respect from people
examples: The students held their professor in high esteem: she was not only a well-known author, but also a wise teacher and a friendly mentor.

meanings: verb: to spread out widely
examples: The food coloring quickly diffused into the water, adding a hint of blue.

meanings: adjective: not wild
examples: The wild horses of the plains were unable to be tamed by anyone but the most experienced handlers.

meanings: adjective: hidden from view; away from people
examples: Although the businessman had to spend most of his time in the crowded city, he preferred living in a secluded cottage in the quiet, empty countryside.
